rows.text: You can install uv on a Mac using MacPorts with the command `$ sudo port install uv`, or on Linux using MacPorts if applicable [2].
You can check if your lockfile is up-to-date by passing the `--check` flag to `uv lock`, which will verify if the lockfile matches the project metadata [2].

You can include extras in the `--from` option to run a tool with extras, like `mypy[faster-cache,reports]`, during a `uvx` command, but for `uv run`, the documentation does not specify a way to add extras directly for just one run [2].
By default, `uv sync` performs "exact" syncing, which means it will remove any packages that are not selected for installation [1].

You can declare dependencies inside a script using inline metadata, which is added at the top of the script with a `script` section using TOML format, and then use `uv add --script` to declare them [1].
You can set the `default-groups` to `"all"` in your `pyproject.toml` file to make uv include all dependency groups by default [1].

On macOS you can install uv via MacPorts with `sudo port install uv` [2].

Use `uvx` with the `--with` (or `-w`) option to specify the extra package when you run the tool, e.g. `uvx --with <extra-package> <tool>` [1]. This adds the package only for that invocation.

Set `default-groups = "all"` in the `[tool.uv]` section of your `pyproject.toml` to have uv include every dependency group by default [1].

Yes – by default `uv sync` performs an “exact” sync and will delete any packages that aren’t listed in your project’s lockfile or `pyproject.toml` [1]. If you want to keep those extra packages, run it with the `--inexact` flag [1].

You can declare dependencies directly in the script by adding an inline metadata block at the top, for example:

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = [
#   "requests<3",
#   "rich",
# ]
# ///
```

Then run the script with `uv run example.py`, and uv will automatically create an isolated environment with those packages installed. [1]
Set the `default-groups` option to `"all"` in your `pyproject.toml` so that uv will include every group when syncing or running. This is shown in the docs as `default-groups = "all"` [1].
